clinician.final_diagnosis: Class V lupus nephritis with idiopathic CD4 lymphocytopenia (ICL)
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 35-year-old male presented with a 6-month history of foamuria and progressive generalized edema indicating nephrotic syndrome, accompanied by verrucous hyperplasia on limbs and face. Initial labs showed profound CD4 lymphocytopenia (CD4 count 30/uL, CD4/CD8 ratio 0.18), supporting immunodeficiency consistent with ICL. Renal biopsy confirmed class V lupus nephritis. Serologic markers were positive for ANA (1:100), anti-dsDNA antibodies (25.4 IU), and showed low C3 complement, supporting systemic lupus erythematosus. Physical exam confirmed severe pitting edema and verrucous skin lesions without other SLE physical manifestations. Imaging showed normal kidney size. During one-year follow-up, disease progression included deep vein embolism, acute kidney injury, and cytomegalovirus viremia, with persistent proteinuria and worsening lesions. Treatment with belimumab led to improved renal function, partial proteinuria remission, subdued lupus activity, stable skin warts, although CD4 counts remained low, confirming persistent immunodeficiency.
